title: Salts - 123 school
heading: Salts
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Into which three chemical groups can we divide all substances on earth?
What is the chemical formula of water?
To which of the 3 chemical groups does water belong? Can you name another substance in this group?
questions.a: Molecular substances. For example polymers, oxygen gas O<sub>2</sub> (g), hydrogen gas H<sub>2</sub> (g)

questions.q: Solid, liquid, gas and dissolved in water: how do you show this in a chemical formula?
Salts consist of charged particles. What do we call them?
Which charges do you always find in salts?
questions.a: Positive + and negative − charge (cations and anions respectively)

questions.q: Can salts conduct electric current?
questions.a: Yes, when they are dissolved in water. Not in solid, crystal form.

questions.q: What colour is Cu<sup>2+</sup> (aq)?
How do you show in a chemical formula that iron has a charge of 3+?
Give the chemical formula of solid calcium chloride
What is the charge of chloride, bromide and iodide ions?
What is the charge of most metal ions?
What is the charge of K and Na ions?
What is the charge of the atoms in group 18, the noble gases?
questions.a: These atoms do not occur in salts and therefore have 0 charge

questions.q: How many mL is one L?
How many grams is 1 kg?
Which separation method can you choose to obtain a dissolved solid salt from a liquid?
questions.a: Evaporation, or precipitating it with another salt so that the salt of interest, or the unwanted salt, precipitates, and then purifying by settling and/or filtering

questions.q: Explain what a saturated solution of table salt is
questions.a: A solution in which the maximum amount of table salt per litre has dissolved and in which extra salt that is added will not dissolve

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of table salt?
How do you write dissolved table salt as a chemical formula?
What is the density of gold? (use BINAS table 15)
questions.a: 19.30 g/cm<sup>3</sup> (look it up in BINAS table 15)

questions.q: 1mL is 1 cm<sup>3</sup>, 1 cm<sup>2</sup> of 1 dm<sup>3</sup>?
Describe what a crystal lattice is
questions.a: In a crystal lattice the positive and negative ions of a salt are arranged systematically.

questions.q: Is the total charge of a salt positive, negative or neutral?
questions.a: The total charge of a salt is always zero/neutral, because the positive and negative charges cancel each other out exactly

questions.q: How does the electrical conductivity change if you add more salt to a salt solution?
questions.a: It increases with the concentration of salt

questions.q: Which two types of ions do most salts consist of?
Which ion always comes first in the formula of a salt?
questions.a: The metal ion, e.g. it is NaCl and not ClNa

questions.q: How can you make salt crystals dissolve faster?
questions.a: By making them finer (more contact surface) or by raising the temperature

questions.q: How can you influence the solubility of certain salts?
questions.a: For a large group of salts the solubility increases with temperature. This is not the case for all salts and depends on the type of salt

questions.q: In which BINAS table do you find the solubility of salts?
Salts of which more than 10 g per litre dissolves are called very soluble/moderately soluble/poorly soluble?
What is the concentration of 12 grams of a salt in 2.5 litres of water?
questions.a: The concentration in g/L is 12/2.5 = 4.8 g/L

questions.q: What is the concentration in g/L of 200 mg of a salt in 2.5 mL?
What are the names of chlorine, bromine and fluorine ions in a salt formula?
questions.a: Chloride, bromide, fluoride, for example sodium chloride

questions.q: Which two metal ions can have a charge of 3+?
questions.a: Fe(III) of Fe<sup>3+</sup> en Al(III) of Al<sup>3+</sup>

questions.q: What do you call an oxygen ion and a sulfur ion in a salt formula?
questions.a: oxide and sulfide, for example iron(III) oxide

questions.q: Give the formula of the salt magnesium chloride
questions.a: MgCl<sub>2</sub> (note: it is Mg<sup>2+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup>, so you need two chloride ions to neutralise the magnesium charge)

questions.q: Give the formula of the salt iron(III) oxide
questions.a: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> (note: it is Fe<sup>3+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup>, so you need two iron ions and 3 oxide ions to form a neutral salt)

Give the chemical formula of the polyatomic ammonium ion
Give the chemical formula of the polyatomic sulfate ion
Give the formula of the salt ammonium sulfate (pay attention to the neutrality of the salt)
What is the charge of chromium in the salt CrCl<sub>3</sub>?
What is the charge of the polyatomic phosphate ion?
Give the chemical formula of the hydroxide ion
Which salts are all very soluble?
questions.a: Salts of Na<sup>+</sup>, K<sup>+</sup>, NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> and NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>
